messages:
maria (oncall): alert fired: token-ttft-p99 > 1.2s for west2-gpu-pool, large token bursts since 09:12 UTC :eyes:
deploy-bot: [ALERT] token-ttft-p99-west2 firing (severity=high) — 12 evals over 5m
ajay: saw that — p99 jump correlates with tokens/sec spike and queue depth rising, can someone grab a prometheus slice?
lia: running quick promql now, looks like queue depth spiked ~09:11 and stayed elevated for ~3m
lia: promql: sum(rate(request_queue_length{pool="west2-gpu"}[1m])) by (shard)  → shows shard-7 and shard-2 flare
dave: also seeing KV cache miss rate increase on same hosts, could be cache eviction storm after a GC?
maria (oncall): logs show a flurry of long-running requests with big prefixes, maybe client workload changed? attaching tail: ```
2026-03-20T09:11:03Z host=shard-7 req_id=... model=gpt-open-16k tokens=980 prefix_len=880 duration_ms=1250
2026-03-20T09:11:08Z host=shard-2 req_id=... model=gpt-open-16k tokens=1200 prefix_len=1100 duration_ms=1430
```
ajay: hunch: large prefixes bypass prefix-cache and force KV cache churn → increased mem pressure → slower attention kernel reads → token p99 up
lia: dug into kvcache metrics: kvcache_miss_rate{host=~"shard-7|shard-2"} jumped from 2% to 18% at 09:10
dave: also noticed network retransmits on egress NIC for those hosts around same time, maybe noisy switch? netdev_errs and rx_packets dropped
maria (oncall): should we mute the high-noise alert and add a correlated alert on kvcache_miss + egress_retransmits so we don't page on benign single-metric flaps?
ajay: yes, propose composite alert: token-ttft-p99>1s AND kvcache_miss_rate>8% AND avg_tcp_retransmits>50 over 3m — reduces false positives from warmup bursts
lia: will draft the promql and grafana panel annotation. promql (kv miss): avg_over_time(kvcache_miss_rate{pool="west2-gpu"}[3m]) > 0.08
lia: promql (tcp): increase(rate(tcp_retransmits_total{instance=~"shard-.*"}[1m])) > 50
dave: for dashboards, add stacked line panel: p50/p95/p99 TTFT + tokens/sec + kvcache_miss_rate aligned, and add per-shard heatmap so we can spot a small set of noisy shards
maria (oncall): curious on cost angle — if long tails keep happening we might need conservative autoscaling to shed low-priority requests instead of paying token cost + p99 spikes
ajay: agree — add a routing rule for large-prefix requests to lower-priority pool, but need product ok. I'll open a ticket with product for traffic-class policy
lia: quick fix: add an annotation in grafana for the 09:11 incident and create a 1h alert suppression window for deployments hitting >75% burst of tokens/sec so deploys don't noisy-alert
maria (oncall): can someone run a packet capture on shard-7 for 10s to validate retransmits? also capture ethtool stats
dave: running tcpdump now, 10s capture -> uploading to /tmp/pcap-shard7-2409876543.pcap.gz
deploy-bot: runbook link: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/token-p99 — recommended steps: check kvcache, check net, check shard queue, scale pools
ajay: PR for alert rule drafted, pinging infra owners for review. Also adding runbook steps into alert description so pager knows next steps
maria (oncall): thanks team — main action items: (1) Ajay finalize composite alert PR, (2) Lia update dashboard with stacked panels + per-shard heatmap, (3) Dave upload pcap & NIC stats to incident thread, (4) Ajay create product ticket for routing for large-prefix traffic. Will follow up in 30m
lia: added grafana annotation at 09:11 with tags {incident:token-ttft-west2,kv-spike} :white_check_mark:
ajay: PR link: https://git.internal/infra/alerts/pulls/842 — request review from @dave @maria
dave: reviewed, left one comment about query cardinality, otherwise LGTM
maria (oncall): closing loop — alert suppressed for 1h while we tune, will re-enable afterwards and monitor. putting notes in the SLO board. :thumbsup:
